Issue No.2 12.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.
So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned

,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
13. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

sentences.text: A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
MACT No.367/2018 SHAILENDER Page 7  SHAILENDER MALIK  MALIK Date: 2024.06.07  16:44:25 +0530

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:
15.
Petitioner/injured (PW1) in his deposition stated that after the accident he was taken to Safdarjung Hospital.
During cross examination PW1 stated that he remained in Safdarjung Hospital for one day and thereafter he was shifted to Cosmos Hospital, Karkari Mor and was discharged after 9-10 days.
Petitioner has proved medical treatment record and medical bills as Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/ZZQ (colly.).

Perusal of these medical documents including bills show that these are the bills of OPD charges, consultation charges, medicine/pharmacy charges and various procedures done, the total of which comes out to be Rs.73,693/-.

There is no dispute with regard to the bills as proved by the petitioner in his deposition as nothing has been asked on this aspect in the cross examination except a suggestion that such medical bills are false and fabricated.

16. Although during the course of arguments ld. Counsel for petitioner made more claim regarding medical expenses, however this Tribunal has to go in accordance with evidence and documents proved on MACT No.367/2018 SHAILENDER Page 8 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.06.07 16:44:35 +0530
the record.
In the evidence of PW1 in para 14 petitioner mentioned expenses of medication of Rs.2,79,949/-.
Such claim of expenses of medication etc. is not substantiated by any documentary/pharmacy bills.
All the bills proved on the record have been duly taken into consideration.

There are certain copy of medical documents lying on the judicial record which have not been exhibited or proved as per law, therefore cannot be taken into consideration when not even exhibited in evidence.
Petitioner has proved medical treatment record and bills in his evidence as Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/ZZQ.
Perusal of these bills substantiate claim of petitioner as deposed by him in his evidence.
As such compensation for a sum of Rs.73,693/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Future medical expenses 17.

Counsel for the petitioner during the arguments has put reliance on document Ex.PW1/ZZQ for claim of future medical expenses as it is submitted that the crush injury of the petitioner though has been healed however plastic surgeon has opined for plastic surgery of the foot of the petitioner, the estimate cost of which is Rs.1,30,000/-.
18.

Having considered such submissions and the evidence of the petitioner, first of all it be noted that in the entire affidavit of examination in chief of petitioner, nowhere it is testified that any plastic surgery has been prescribed by the doctor, the estimate cost of which is of Rs.1,30,000/-.
No doubt in the evidence this document Ex.PW1/ZZQ has been referred but mere exhibition of one document is not proof of that fact.
That document simply mentions that one Dr.Manoj Bansal has prescribed for plastic surgery but document Ex.PW1/ZZQ is not the opinion/ prescription of same Dr.Manoj Bansal.
It is signed by authorized signatory of Cosmos Super Specialty Hospital.

The said authorized signatory has MACT No.367/2018 SHAILENDER Page 9 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.06.07 16:44:42 +0530 also not appeared in the witness box for proving the document Dar - Saurabh vs Sahil on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12239247/
6 and the opinion of Dr.Manoj Bansal as stated in that document.
Therefore when evidence of petitioner is completely silent, no doctor has been examined for proving such future medical expense or plastic surgery etc.
Mere exhibition of a document Ex.PW1/ZZQ cannot be a sole basis for awarding sum of Rs.1,30,000/- for future medical expenses.
Accordingly such claim is declined.

Loss of earning during treatment:
19.

It has come in the evidence of PW1/Sourab that at the time of accident he was student of B.Com second year, due to accident he could not appear in the examination for B.Com second year and suffered huge academic loss.

It is also on the record that in additional evidence PW1 when again appeared in the witness box on 26.09.2023 filed additional affidavit and documents showing that he completed his graduation from University of Delhi in year 2019 as well as thereafter completed B.Lib. From IGNOU in the year 2021.

The documents of those academic certificates are Ex.PW1/ZZR to Ex.PW1/ZZT.
20.

From the above evidence of petitioner it is evident that on the date of accident i.e. 30.04.2018 petitioner was studying in third semester of B.Com. and according to petitioner he completed his B.Com degree in 2019.
As such except for a delay of around six months, petitioner could complete his graduation even after the accident.
Moreover petitioner thereafter pursued for B.Lib from Open University which was also completed by him in 2021.
Petitioner in his evidenced claimed compensation on account of expenditure involved for examination not attended of Rs.3,500/-.

In such circumstance this Tribunal taking into consideration that at the time of accident petitioner was major, his notional MACT No.367/2018 by SHAILENDER Page 10 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.06.07 16:44:54 +0530
income is assessed at parity with minimum wages of a graduate worker in Delhi which is Rs.18,332/- per month.

Since his completion of graduation/B.Com delayed by six months approximately on account of accident, petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is entitled for compensation under the above mentioned head of Rs.1,13,492/- (Rs.18,332 X 6 months + Rs.3,500).

Loss of future earning due to disability :
21.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) Whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;

(iii) If the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.

sentences.text: If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.

But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain MACT No.367/2018 Digitally signed by Page 11 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.06.07 16:45:02 +0530 its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.
13.

We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of MACT No.367/2018 Digitally signed by Page 12 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.06.07 16:45:11 +0530 permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence,
concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).

22.
Petitioner has admittedly suffered medical disability to the extent of 27% in relation to right lower limb as proved bby Dr.Vikramajeet Singh from GTB Hospital.
23. This Tribunal has to assess the medical disability as well as functional disability of the petitioner to assess future earning capacity and loss of income.
In this regard ld.

sentences.text: In this case petitioner at the time of accident was a student and pursuing for B.Com.
It is admitted fact that even after the accident petitioner completed his B.Com degree in 2019 and thereafter also completed B.Lib in 2021.
Permanent disability is in relation to right lower limb to the extent of 27%.

Considering the nature of education and future pursuits, this Tribhnal finds that half of the medical disability can be taken to the functional disability of the petitioner i.e. 13.5% for the purpose of deciding the amount of compensation under the above mentioned head.
25. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr. (supra)].

As such age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e. 30.04.2018 was 18 years.

As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 18 as applicable to age group between 15 to 20 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.

As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed as Rs.18,332/- + 40% (Rs.18,332 + Rs.7,333), total Rs.25,665/-.

Thus applying the functional disability to be 13.5% of Rs.25,665/-,
amount comes out to be Rs.3,465/-.
As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.3,465 X 12 X 18 = Rs.7,48,440/-.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
27.

Since it has come on record that petitioner suffered grievous injuries on different parts of his body and as per medical documents, this Tribunal awarded compensation under the head of loss of earning during treatment for a period of six months.
It has also come in the evidence of petitioner that he had continuously taken treatment from different hospitals.

Therefore this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that petitioner must have incurred expenses towards special diet for his well being during the period of treatment and also incurred expenses towards going to different hospitals.
Thus this Tribunal awards compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of special diet and Rs.20,000/- under the head of conveyance charges to the petitioner.

Attendant Charges:
28.
Petitioner in this case has claimed attendant charges also.

Although this Tribunal has already decided while deciding the question of compensation on the ground of loss of income and that petitioner his education loss for about six months as he could complete his B.Com in 2019 whereas he was in second year of B.Com at the time of accident.
Considering the nature of injuries, this Tribunal has already assessed that petitioner must have taken treatment for about six months.
In such circumstance attendant charges can also be decided on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled worker.
In this regard petitioner has evidence

MACT No.367/2018 by SHAILENDER Page 15 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.06.07 16:45:33 +0530 one witness PW3 Mangal Sing who has stated that he was given stipend of Rs.7,500/- per month for three months in cash, the receipts of which are Ex.PW3/A to Ex.PW3/C.
Accordingly in view of the evidence of PW1 as well as PW3, petitioner is entitled for Rs.22,500/- (Rs.7,500 X 3 months) towards attendant charges.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
29.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
